thread:
olivia: Anyone else seeing a sudden tail-latency bump on continuous-batcher this morning? p95 -> p99 looks bad since ~03:10 UTC
raj: yep noticed it on prod dashboards, spike ~03:08-03:20, throughput steady but tails jump to 600-900ms on some models
maria: attaching quick snapshot: p50 45ms, p95 210ms, p99 880ms for model-ggml-13b-v2 around that window
devon: do we have any recent changes to the scheduler or kernel selector? I rolled a micropatch to allocator yesterday but it was just a refactor
olivia: no config changes in rollout log, deploy-bot shows no deployments to serving runtime in that timeframe
infra-bot: deploy-bot: no deployments to `serving-runtime` between 2026-03-17 02:00 and 2026-03-17 04:00 UTC
logan: I pulled traces, interesting pattern: a subset of requests got routed to a GPU pool with older kernel ABI, then fell back to fused-kernel path after 150ms, causing long tail. Might be kernel-selector flip under pressure
raj: hmm kernel flip + KV cache miss could explain it. Any KV cache eviction storms in same window?
maria: yes, KV cache eviction rate spiked on shard-gpu-7 at 03:09. Evictions/sec from 20 -> 120 for ~6min. Logs show many `kvcache: evict key due to memory_pressure` entries
devon: I ran a quick correlation: microbatch size distribution shifted — more 1-2 token microbatches for that shard. Continuous-batcher admission seemed to under-batch leading to higher kernel-switch frequency
olivia: can you paste the profiler heap/cpu sample? wondering if kernel selection path is hot
logan: pasted flamegraph link: https://internal-graphs/fg/207890-evict. Key hotspot is `kernel_selector::select_for_request` and `kvcache::lookup_miss_path`
raj: hypothesis: small microbatches + high miss rate cause the runtime to try fused kernels, then fallback, causing double work and KV churn. Also admission controller oscillation might thrash packing decisions
maria: I captured a short log segment:
[03:09:12.112] admission: accept batch size=2 shard=shard-gpu-7
[03:09:12.115] kvcache: lookup miss key=ctx-9e4f
[03:09:12.116] kernel_selector: chose kernel=fused_attn_v1 for seq_len=128
[03:09:12.265] kernel_fallback: fused_attn_v1 -> scalar_attn_v2 (fallback latency 149ms)
[03:09:12.266] kvcache: evict key=ctx-1a2b cause=mem_press

devon: that fallback latency is suspiciously consistent with the p99 tail. We need to know why fused_attn_v1 is being picked for those requests. Maybe the kernel scorer thresholds were tuned for larger microbatches and degrade for small ones
olivia: is there metric for kernel-selector score distribution?
logan: yes, `kernel_scores.hist` shows a bimodal behavior; score favored fused for seq_len>=64, but after recent input distribution shift (more short prompts) it still favored fused due to stale sample window
raj: so stale scoring + microburst of short prompts = bad pick + cache miss = eviction storms. Can we short-circuit to probability-based selector for now? fallback to always pick scalar_attn_v2 for seq_len < 64 on shard-gpu-7 as mitigation
maria: I can push a hotfix config to override selector on that shard, low risk. Will also increase kvcache max_entries temporarily to reduce evictions
devon: +1 for temporary config. Also we should adjust admission controller hysteresis to avoid oscillation — increase min-pack-window from 8ms to 20ms so we get slightly larger microbatches
olivia: sounds good. Maria, please do the selector override and kvcache bump. Devon/Logan follow with admission change and monitor. I'll own the postmortem notes
maria: pushing override now: `curl -X POST https://admin/selector/override -d '{"shard":"shard-gpu-7","rule":"prefer:scalar_attn_v2 if seq_len<64"}'`
infra-bot: config-change-bot: selector override applied to shard-gpu-7 by maria at 2026-03-17T03:32:15Z
logan: kvcache max_entries increased from 120k -> 300k on shard-gpu-7 and shard-gpu-8; eviction rate dropped back to baseline in ~45s
raj: admission hysteresis patch submitted: `raise_min_pack_window=20ms` in PR 4892, staging tests pass, promoting to canary in 10m
devon: rolling canary for admission window now to 10% of serving fleet
maria: after override + cache bump, p99 dropped below 250ms across affected models. still watching for weird regressions
olivia: great. action items: (1) devon/logan follow up on admission hysteresis tuning (2) engineering: add kernel-selector scoring TTL so it adapts faster to input distribution (3) perf: add a test that simulates microburst of short prompts to catch this in CI
raj: I'll add an eval for short-prompt microbursts and include KV cache metrics in regression alerts
logan: note: need to also fix kvcache accounting bug that underreports memory pressure, opened issue #7721
maria: thanks all. I'll document the incident and timeline in incident runbook
olivia: thanks team :thumbsup: we should keep this thread pinned to the incident channel for follow-ups
